# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — generated timing data in `buildScripts/util/e2eEngineDurations.json`, the selector's only input; no code path changes.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The table now carries the candidate's measured durations, including the two new specs (the Desktop tear-out and Calendar Basic), and the production allocator still assigns all 324 specs once across 15 shards. Verified on `280ea74202`: this head's own Engine Tests run 45127168628 passed every shard. Its slowest steps were 358 s (5/15), 352 s (14/15) and 342 s (13/15 and 11/15), all under the unchanged 360 s deadline, where attempts 1 and 2 on `8e649faff9` overran shards 1 and 13. What I looked for was margin, and there is little: 2 s on shard 5, while your first repair run put shard 3 at 356 s. The post-merge candidate run (AC-4) can therefore still overrun one shard on run-to-run variance. For the cut, the remedy is a failed-jobs re-run, since a timeout is not a test failure. A structural margin, a 16th shard or a changed deadline, is a post-cut decision for the operator, made with these numbers.

**Findings:** None.
